A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GeCo3D research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable, and relocated or renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original shape-matching accuracy, Dirichlet energies, runtime measurements, coupling/feature ablations and qualitative partial-shape and planar-graph experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds discretisation sensitivity, constraint-memory measurements and quantitative partial-to-full matching results.

M1.justification: The coupled surface-cycle formulation, matching costs, LP relaxation, distortion bound k=2 and problem-size reduction are retained. The corrected injectivity-matrix expression includes target self-edges already allowed in v1, so it does not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Appendix D.1 adds an unequal-discretisation test scenario, fixing one mesh at 1,000 triangles while varying the other. The datasets and principal tasks remain unchanged; SHREC’16 partial-to-full matching was already evaluated qualitatively in v1.

E2.justification: v3 Table 7 introduces ULRSSM and SpiderMatch as comparators for partial-to-full SHREC’16 matching, where v1 showed only the proposed method’s qualitative results. The existing full-shape and runtime comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include a five-instance FAUST discretisation sweep with one mesh fixed at 1,000 triangles and constraint-memory comparisons at 500, 1,000, 1,500 and 2,000 faces. v3 also applies the existing accuracy and Dirichlet-energy metrics quantitatively to SHREC’16 cuts. Retained experiments show no substantive setting changes.

E4.justification: v3 adds a focused sensitivity analysis of matching accuracy under unequal mesh discretisations (Appendix D.1, Fig. A.5). The coupling/feature ablation in Table 5 and existing qualitative failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report runtime medians over five shape pairs without adding seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The five instances used in the new discretisation study specify evaluation sample size, rather than repeated-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 3–5 and existing result plots retain their values. New Table 7 reports SHREC’16 geodesic errors of 0.062 for ours, 0.071 for ULRSSM and 0.066 for SpiderMatch. Table 6 adds constraint-memory results, including 1.2 GB for ours versus 3.1 GB for Windheuser et al. and 4.0 GB for SpiderMatch at 2,000 faces. Fig. A.5 adds discretisation-dependent errors.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds an explicit equal-genus assumption. The injectivity matrix S is corrected from using E_Y to the extended edge set E_Y^+ (v1 Eq. 3; v3 Eq. 4). The product-graph definition moves from Appendix B.1 into the main text; the geometric-consistency lemma and proof remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution bullets retain the claims of practical scalability, global optimality and geometric consistency through coupled surface cycles and hypergraph flow, together with a planar-graph proof of concept. The conclusion’s added learning-related statement is prospective positioning.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly states equal genus as an applicability condition for its geometric-consistency setting, which v1 did not state. Existing limitations concerning collapsed matchings, inside-out flips and unresolved polynomial-time solvability are retained.

D1.justification: v3 newly supplies a code-access link and states public availability in the abstract. It also corrects the hardware description from 128 GB GDDR5 to DDR5 RAM. The solver version, distortion bound and matrix-reduction details were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: The bibliography adds four works concerning total unimodularity, circuits and integer optimisation. SpiderMatch’s formulation is described more precisely, and the conclusion adds prospective positioning toward geometric consistency in learning-based methods. The main related-work argument remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 makes local terminology and prose edits, expands explanations of SpiderMatch and the constraint matrices, and moves the product-graph definition from Appendix B.1 to Section 4.2.1. The overall narrative and section hierarchy are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 6–7 and the discretisation plot, resizes and relocates existing illustrations, and incorporates text and results alongside previously isolated appendix figures. Figure 9 changes from vertically stacked to side-by-side examples. Existing result panels remain present despite renumbering.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens practical validation by supplementing v1’s qualitative partial-to-full evidence with quantitative comparisons and adding discretisation sensitivity and constraint-memory measurements. The code-access link and mathematical clarifications also improve usability. These are limited but concrete gains; the central results and unresolved questions about LP integrality and computational complexity remain unchanged.
